about: The ECB bank lending survey stage-1 reply of 29 October 2026 (brief-s1-bb6e90d11da0c717, HTTP 200, validated under brief-evidence-3) as a regression fixture, copied from the saved records by data/local-checks/net-balance-prose/make_fixture.py. reply.change_text: In the ECB's October 2026 bank lending survey, euro area banks reported a further net tightening of credit standards for loans to firms ({f1}) and a net decrease in demand for loans to firms ({f2}) and for housing loans ({f3}) in the third quarter of 2026.

facts.text: The ECB's October 2026 BLS says euro area banks reported a further net tightening of credit standards for loans to firms in Q3 2026 (net percentage 9%, above the 5% expected), unchanged for housing loans (0%) and tighter for consumer credit (14%).
Banks reported a net decrease in loan demand from firms (-6%), housing loans (-27%) and consumer credit (-2%) in Q3 2026; the ECB says higher interest rates were the main driver of the declines.

Several banks expect a gradual but sustained increase in loan demand to finance AI digital infrastructure, particularly data centres. Most have no specific quantitative criteria for AI-related lending.
Banks' access to retail funding deteriorated, the largest fall since the series began in 2011. The survey ran 21 September to 6 October 2026 with 159 banks and a 100% response rate.

reports.title: October 2026 euro area bank lending survey
reports.excerpt:
According to the October 2026 bank lending survey (BLS), euro area banks reported a further net tightening of credit standards – banks’ internal guidelines or loan approval criteria – for loans or credit lines to enterprises in the third quarter of 2026 (net percentage of 9% of banks; Chart 1).
In the third quarter of 2026, euro area banks reported a net decrease in demand for loans or credit lines to firms (net percentage of -6%; Chart 2).
Banks reported a strong net decrease in demand for housing loans (net percentage of -27%), which was a more pronounced decline than in the second quarter (-15%) and exceeded the expectations reported by banks in the previous survey round (-12%).
- Decline in loan demand across all segments, driven mainly by higher interest rates
Increases in interest rates were the main driver of the decline, followed by falling consumer confidence and worsening housing market prospects.
